resposta:

**Reasoning:**

The narrative unfolds in the following order:

4. **Ruwen summons an Arcane Maelstrom and directs it at Ceplotryn** (Narrative 4).

Therefore, the correct order is 2, 3, 1, 4.

 PROLOGUE Lalquinrial sat on an ancient throne of solid gold, buried deep underground and hidden for millennia. The architecture caused nostalgia to surface along with a sense of peace. None of this matters, Nameless said. It is but a reflection of a lie and holds no value to us. Lalquinrial didn’t respond but acknowledged the truth of Nameless’ words. The creature had reignited Lalquinrial’s purpose and focused him like he’d never experienced. The clarity of purpose had set him free. Exhaustion kept Lalquinrial on the throne, and Abaddon and Zadkiel stood guard, protecting him from any of the dangers that might emerge from the depths below this palace. Soon he hoped to regain his strength and handle Nameless and the Inquisitor by himself. Lalquinrial glanced at Abaddon and Zadkiel who stood on either side of the throne. He’d known them back in the old days and had always wondered what had happened to them. Now he knew the Destruction Realm had cleansed the two angels, turning them into Knights of Destruction. The Inquisitor had tried to speed Lalquinrial’s absorption of Destruction Essence as well, attempting to turn him into a mindless husk like the two Archangels. Nameless had risen to the threat, matching the attack with his own zealousness. That protection, along with Lalquinrial’s own Soul Power, had proved too much for the Inquisitor. Miranda had imprisoned the Inquisitor for thousands of years in her Black Pyramid, so he couldn’t blame the priest for wanting to convert Lalquinrial’s flesh into darkness. Lalquinrial’s victory only served to validate his existence. In this grand illusion, he had once again proven he held enough truth to survive and continue. Lalquinrial had reached a balance, now. His left arm and legs had turned into black destruction essence, while his torso and head remained unblemished. Nameless continually battled the advancing darkness, taking pressure off Lalquinrial and giving him time to build his mental strength. Eventually, he would become strong enough to regain control of his body. Three entities in one body, all fighting for supremacy over the others. Lalquinrial didn’t bother speaking with either of the Archangels, as after all this time they’d lost most of their identity. They’d become creatures of desire and only wanted to consume. The Inquisitor had the same desire but retained logic and self-control. Even though the Darkness only infected three of Lalquinrial’s limbs, he felt the hunger for destruction. It had given him a better understanding of the creatures he dealt with. Lalquinrial found it ironic that Nameless, the Inquisitor, and his own desires fought each other for control, even though they all had the same goal. Same goals but different paths, and Lalquinrial preferred the route that kept his identity whole. Afterall, what value would finding the truth hold if he hadn’t retained his free will and intelligence. Things had never looked better. The Destruction Essence in Lalquinrial’s body protected him against most forms of power, including Spirit, and his Divine brothers and sisters no longer posed a threat to him. The battle waging inside him had forced a vast increase in his mental strength. Every moment brought him closer to regaining full control of himself. The Inquisitor and its kind had benefited from this relationship as well. Their weakness in the Material Realm had made recovering from the sudden disappearance of Spirit impossible and uncountable Inquisitors remained stranded in the Darkness. Now that Lalquinrial understood their origin, purpose, and abilities he had devised a possible solution. The Destruction Essence invading Lalquinrial’s body allowed him to communicate with the Inquisitor and if Lalquinrial understood correctly, a reservoir of power existed in the deepest part of the Destruction Realm, what he’d always called the Shadow Realm. It contained the magic that the Inquisitors had stripped from the Universe before Pen had stopped their advance by hiding all the Spirit. Lalquinrial had convinced the Inquisitor he planned to help them utilize this reservoir of power to restart the Darkness. In truth he still contemplated the reservoir’s revelation and wondered about alternate possibilities. Perhaps this reservoir would allow him to break free from this tidal pool immediately and permit him to swim in the true ocean of the Outerverse. Using the reservoir in such a fashion would allow Lalquinrial to reach his ultimate goal, escape, much faster, but the destructive needs of both Nameless and the Inquisitor rebelled at such ideas. The creatures both yearned to annihilate this universe. Nameless, because it represented a lie, and the Inquisitor, because destruction embodied its purpose. The third possibility was completing the Harbinger quest, which, depending on how long each quest step took, might be quicker. Distortion requires destruction, Nameless reminded Lalquinrial. All other paths are false. Only annihilation reveals the truth. “I know,” Lalquinrial whispered. The new quests had arrived a little too late for Lalquinrial anyway. While they unlocked routes to great power, that power interfered with his current form. Perhaps once he controlled both Nameless and the Destruction Essence in his body, he could turn his attention to finding a compatible quest path that harnessed all these new Outerverse abilities while allowing him to retain his Destruction Essence progress. Lalquinrial turned his thoughts to the recent battle with Starfield. Nameless had provided the means to deliver Lalquinrial a great victory, and the creature still rejoiced at the demise of its maker. Starfield had allowed his most critical vulnerability—emotional ties—to fatally trap him. Those relationships had anchored Starfield to that vaporizing planet, and his attempts to rescue his friends would have either delayed him sufficiently for the crossing ring explosion to engulf him, or if he did manage to escape, the guilt of leaving his friends behind would devastate him. Not long ago, Lalquinrial’s response to Starfield’s fall would have mirrored the joy Nameless felt. Now though, things felt less personal. He was Lightbringer, and he carried the truth. His battle encompassed so much more than a single boy. Despite Starfield’s tenacity and obvious ability, he fought to preserve an illusion. He didn’t want the dream to end. Starfield deserved pity, and a chance to embrace the truth. Lalquinrial, mindful of Starfield’s weaknesses, possessed far fewer personal vulnerabilities and had already begun the process of detaching himself from them. Simandreial had criticized him for his bond with Nameless and the Destruction Essence, arguing he had forfeited too much of his identity. She never supported you, Nameless whispered. She did not see the truth. Lies, in all their forms, must be purged. “I know,” Lalquinrial responded. And yet you continue to clutch one⁠— “Enough!” Lalquinrial screamed and his fingers dug into the soft gold of the throne’s armrests. Nameless thrashed wildly in displeasure, and Lalquinrial closed his eyes, enduring the onslaught. It became a little easier each time. Despite the overpowering urges of Nameless and the Destruction Essence to sever all connections to this universe, Lalquinrial still protected his feelings for Echodriel, and he hoped that they could talk soon. For the time being, Lalquinrial needed to stay concealed and disconnected from the universe as he mastered control over his mind and body. Remaining here in the Material Realm posed risks, but the Shadow Realm amplified the Destruction within him, significantly challenging his ability to resist. Once the Inquisitor confirmed the best method to reach the power reservoir’s bottom, Lalquinrial needed to decide on the path to grasping his destiny. A slow inevitable destruction as the Darkness once again crawled across the Universe, or a catastrophic, but not Universe ending, explosion to push Lalquinrial into the arms of the Outerverse. 
 CHAPTER 1 Sift stood in the lower vault of the Black Pyramid, surrounded by sets of legendary armor each displayed to highlight their beauty and craftsmanship. Ignoring all of them, he studied the row of plain Cultivator robes, his face frozen in an uncharacteristic frown. He reached out to touch the closest one, a set the color of freshly plucked leaves. “Don’t touch it,” Fluffy growled. “I just got this place cleaned up from the last miscreant that sneaked in here.” He gave Ruwen a long look. Ruwen raised his eyebrows but decided to hold his tongue. First, Blapy had brought him in here to get his Ink Lord armor, he hadn’t sneaked in. And second, it was his scrubbing-Minions that had cleaned everything in here, including the fingerprints he’d left on his first trip. Sift glanced at Ruwen as well. “Is it your fault that Fluffy is so grouchy today?” “I’m not grouchy,” Fluffy growled again. “I just don’t know why everyone has to touch everything.” “Yeah,” Ruwen agreed giving Sift a serious look. “Why do you have to touch everything? Don’t you know it’s disrespectful?” Fluffy glared at Ruwen. “What?” Ruwen asked. “I’m just agreeing with you. If anyone knows how hard it is to get all this stuff clean, it’s me, right?” Fluffy didn’t seem amused, so Ruwen turned back to Sift, hoping to direct Fluffy away from Ruwen’s previous misdeeds. “Why are you being so picky? What do you want?” Sift studied the robes again, his face returning to the painful expression he’d worn for the past fifteen minutes. “My robes had the color of a perfectly fried doughnut, light brown, an almost golden color that promised just the right amount of resistance when bitten. They were light and airy, like the frosting on a lovingly baked pastry. Just wearing those robes made me feel like an éclair.” “You feel like an éclair?” Ruwen asked. “Have you lost your mind? Clothes are something you just wear.” Sift didn’t look at Ruwen, but he shook a finger in that direction. “You see, that’s why you have so many problems.” “My problems are because I don’t care what I’m wearing?” “Yep,” Sift replied. “The outside is a reflection of the inside. I have a whole list of clothing-related self-help pastries just floating around up here,” he said as he rotated a finger next to his temple. “Darkness take me,” Ruwen replied. “The only thing your self-help pastries will accomplish is driving people to the priests for therapy.” Sift turned his attention to Fluffy. “What do Fluffy’s clothes tell you?” “Oh no, don’t include me in your nonsense,” Fluffy barked. “I regretted bringing you in here ten seconds after I agreed to it, and now I feel like you’re just punishing me. Blapy put you up to this, didn’t she? I thought she’d gotten all her anger out about the alchemy resource incident. Perhaps she doesn’t believe I’ve suffered enough.” “I really appreciate your help with my Alchemy leveling,” Ruwen told Fluffy. “It made an enormous difference, and I know you suffered for helping me. I won’t forget it.” “If you mean that, by all that’s holy, get this madman to pick a set of armor. How hard can it be?” Sift narrowed his eyes as if studying Fluffy. “The vest says organization, the ordered pens, and metal thingies show a mind clean and detailed. Pants sturdy, displaying the man’s dependable work ethic. Boots laced and tied perfectly, each in balance, indicating the importance of planning and a desire to not let sloppy mistakes interfere with his forward movement. I have known Fluffy my whole life, and I have never seen him in different attire. This signifies his commitment to stability, repetition, and efficiency.” Ruwen and Fluffy stared at Sift with shocked expressions. Ruwen had to admit that Sift’s analysis held a lot of merit, and the connections he’d drawn between Fluffy’s clothes, and his behavior were scarily accurate. Instead of saying any of that, he chose a different response. “Lylan and Hamma wrecked your mind with all their fashion talk.” Sift narrowed his eyes in thought as he studied Ruwen. Ruwen held up his hands. “I’m not interested⁠—” Sift pinched the black fabric of Ruwen’s shirt, interrupting him. Ruwen slapped Sift’s hand away. “Stop that.” “You look like a level ten Shade.” Ruwen glanced at his own clothes, which were a set that he’d gotten from the Black Pyramid on his very first trip. It consisted of basic Shade attire, which meant all black, close-fitting, comfortable garments. “What’s wrong with my clothes?” “You’re the glazed doughnut of the pastry world,” Sift responded. “I don’t need to look fancy. All the important stuff is up here,” Ruwen said, tapping his temple. “Yeah, right, it has nothing to do with how it shows off your abs.” Ruwen suppressed the surge of blood to his cheeks. Sift grinned and nodded knowingly. A loud gong sounded behind Ruwen, and he flinched as a seven-year-old blonde girl with pigtails appeared. Blapy turned to Fluffy. “Why are you still here?” Fluffy raised his hands in a helpless gesture and looked between Ruwen and Sift. Blapy sighed and rubbed her forehead. “We were looking at the robes,” Fluffy started, “and then somehow we got on the topic of pastries, and now they’re arguing about psychological fashion.” “That sounds about right,” Blapy said. She turned to Sift. “Hurry up and pick one of these. The pyramid can’t afford to have you tying up its Quartermaster like this.” Sift frowned. “None of these feel right or look right. I’m the Soaring Sage. I need to look regal and, I don’t know, sageful. And all of you can wait patiently because Shelly and I are the only reason the lower vault still exists.” Blapy pinched the bridge of her nose and whispered to herself. “I should have let the whole place explode.” With obvious effort, Blapy calmed herself and studied Sift. After thirty seconds, even Fluffy became a little uncomfortable. “What?” Sift finally asked. “Oh, I’m just contemplating how I’m about to make yet another huge mistake. Something I seem to accomplish with you two daily.” “Headless Pete says mistakes are opportunities if you have a strong mind.” Blapy turned to Ruwen. “Who is Headless Pete?” Sift opened his mouth, his eyes wide with excitement, and Ruwen raised a hand to stop him. “Trust me, you don’t want him to answer that question.” Sift pushed Ruwen’s hand down. “Don’t listen to him. He’s still mad because Headless Pete knew more about turtles.” Blapy turned to Fluffy. “Headless Pete? Turtles? Does any of this make sense to you?” Fluffy gazed between Ruwen and Sift shaking his head slightly. “The longest I’ve ever followed one of their conversations is just under a minute. I thought this was going to be a quick trip to the lower vault, and instead, I have a headache debuff and we’ve made zero progress.” Blapy looked up at Ruwen and Sift, waving a finger between the two. “Be honest with me. Is this an act? How are you capable of confusing everyone you meet within a minute of contact?” Ruwen and Sift faced each other. “You are a little confusing,” Ruwen told Sift. Sift touched his chest. “I’m confusing? How about when you styled your hair with bendy blood? That was like the very first day I met you.” Ruwen pointed at Sift. “That was your fault. I was totally unprepared to fight Rod Spiders, and you just left me by myself.” “Well, I didn’t think you’d bathe in your enemy’s blood. Who does that?” Ruwen touched his hair. It was still on the shorter side and a little spiky, but Hamma had helped him smooth out the roughest portions, and he didn’t think it looked too bad now. “That’s not confusing,” Ruwen said. “It only demonstrates how terrible a teacher you were right from the beginning.” Sift opened his mouth to respond and Blapy screamed. “Stop!” Blapy took a couple of deep breaths. “I give up. I’m done thinking. I’m just going to do it. Darkness take the consequences.” Blapy looked at Fluffy. “Sorry, Quartermaster. I’ve already reached my limit. I’ll find you later.” Blapy disappeared, and a moment later, to Ruwen’s shock, Miranda appeared. Ruwen still didn’t understand how Miranda’s three forms overlapped or interacted with each other. Blapy was almost always the form taken in the dungeon and Miranda’s human form only appeared when things became serious. He’d only seen what he believed to be Blapy’s true form once, and that was during the Step Championship semifinal match with Stump and Chip, where she’d taken the form of a massive black wyrm. Fluffy immediately bowed. “Welcome, goddess. It’s a pleasure to see you.” “Thank you, Quartermaster. I relieve you of this torturous experience.” “Many thanks, goddess.” And Fluffy immediately created a portal and disappeared. Sift spoke to Ruwen. “You just made up with Fluffy, and now you went and irritated him again.” “I wasn’t irritating him. You were, with your talk about pastries and fashion and hairstyles. I don’t even remember why we’re here anymore.” Miranda cleared her throat before Sift could respond, and the pair turned to face the goddess. Sift bowed to Miranda, and Ruwen gave her a shallow bow as well. “Greetings, goddess,” Sift said. “I apologize for my manners. My friend here has discombobulated me.” Ruwen turned back to Sift. “There’s no way you know what ‘discombobulated’ means.” Sift leaned back, offended. Miranda pressed her palms together in front of her lips and groaned. Ruwen and Sift turned their attention back to the goddess. “Do you want some robes or not?” Miranda asked. “Oh, yeah,” Sift replied. “I need new ones. Mine were destroyed by that dumb hydra.” Miranda’s wings partially unfolded, their black canvas filled with galaxies and stars. They disappeared quickly and Ruwen wondered if she was nervous. “Against my better judgment but in recognition of saving this planet, I’m going to give you a special set of Cultivator robes. You’re forbidden to ask any questions about them. Absolutely none.” 
 CHAPTER 2 “So mysterious,” Sift said to Miranda, his voice giving away his excitement. “First, though,” Miranda said, “I want you to equip that tattoo you have in your dimensional belt.” The dimensional belt was the only thing that Sift had salvaged after his clothes dissolved from the hydra acid. “Why now?” Sift asked. “Because I have sympathy for Shelly,” Miranda replied. “Speaking to such an empty-headed buffoon must exhaust her, and this might raise your intelligence enough to spare the Elder Tortoise pain.” Sift glanced at Ruwen. “Buffoon means fool,” Ruwen said. Sift nodded and faced Miranda. “A fool’s tongue speaks to its own reflection.” Ruwen leaned back, stunned at the quick response. Miranda didn’t respond but took on a contemplative expression. “That one,” Sift continued, “is part of the Soaring Sage line of pastries, although I might be convinced to put it in the self-help section.” Miranda slowly shook her head. “Scratch my scales. The pair of you travel so quickly from clowns to genius, it defies understanding. Now equip that tattoo.” Sift slouched and slowly reached into his dimensional belt. Ruwen recalled the item’s description. It had come from the loot they’d taken from the obnoxious table next to them at Pour Judgement. Name: Beastmaster Ink Effect: Enables the wearer to communicate with and understand animals. Strengthens the bond with animal companions. Description: Tattoo’s depiction changes based on the primary bonded companion. “Why are you acting like a baby?” Ruwen asked. “Because I like things the way they are,” Sift whispered. “If Shelly understands me better, she might not like me.” “That’s a very real possibility,” Ruwen said, and when Sift’s head snapped up in alarm, Ruwen grinned and grabbed Sift’s shoulder. “Don’t be stupid. That turtle loves you and would do anything for you. She’s already proven that many times. If anything, what if she has a bunch of recipes she’s been unable to communicate. Like celery muffins, or cilantro cream filled carrot donuts.” Sift widened his eyes. “What if I start liking vegetables or weirder stuff like wanting to rub my body with lettuce. Shelly has a lot of strange behaviors.” “That’s what makes the two of you such a good match.” Sift didn’t look convinced and turned his attention to Miranda. “Maybe I should wait for one of your tattoos? Yours are the best, right?” “Usually, but the Dungeon Core that created that tattoo formed when its bonded human died. And when it comes to bonds, theirs are better, as subtlety is not one of my strengths, and this type of working requires a light touch.” “What will it look like?” “The ones I’ve seen are masterfully done, as the bond can access some memories.” “I miss my snake tattoo.” Ruwen frowned. “Is that really who you are? A snake tattoo guy?” Sift stared at the tattoo with a deep sigh. “I guess not.” He pulled up his shirt and placed the tattoo over his heart. The tattoo sank into Sift’s skin, disappearing from sight. He watched to see what would appear, but nothing happened.” Sift glanced up at Miranda. “It doesn’t happen instantly,” Miranda scolded. “These types of tattoos need to gain an understanding of the current bonds before materializing.” “Maybe you’ll get a shell,” Ruwen said. Sift looked conflicted about that idea. Before Sift could respond, Miranda raised her hands to silence them. “I’ve already reached my limit with you two.” She gave a piercing look at Sift and sighed deeply. “These are very special to me,” her voice lowered, and she spoke softly. “Please take care of them.” Miranda straightened her arms, and a long jacket appeared over her left arm, with pants draped over her right. Her right hand held a pair of thin shoes that reminded Ruwen of socks. The color shimmered between light grey and midnight blue. The long-sleeved jacket looked far too large for Sift. It had a white, flat, stiff collar that protected the back and sides of the neck. The pants and boots shared the same color. Sift gently took the items from Miranda. “They’re beautiful. I love them.” Miranda’s eyes glistened, and she gave a tiny nod. Sift handed the items to Ruwen and began undressing. Ruwen turned to apologize to Miranda for Sift’s behavior, but the goddess had disappeared. The garments had generated notifications and Ruwen opened them curiously. Why had these clothes caused so much emotion in Miranda? Name: Void Jacket Set Bonus (3-Piece): Universal Resonance – attracted toward nearest Universe. Physical Armor Class: 1,500 Spiritual Armor Class: 2,000 Quality: Mythical Durability: 100,000,000 of 100,000,000 Effect (Passive): Void Whisper – the stillness of the Void reveals whispers of danger. Description: Blue grey long jacket with a stiff collar. Only Abyssal Lords can survive, navigate, and alter the void. This jacket, through long use, has absorbed an Abyssal Lord’s power. Name: Void Pants Set Bonus (3-Piece): Universal Resonance – attracted toward nearest Universe. Physical Armor Class: 1,000 Spiritual Armor Class: 1,500 Quality: Mythical Durability: 100,000,000 of 100,000,000 Effect (Passive): Void Guard – the stillness of the Void quiets nearby energy by 50%. Description: Blue grey pants. Only Abyssal Lords can survive, navigate, and alter the void. These pants, through long use, have absorbed an Abyssal Lord’s power. Name: Void Slippers Set Bonus (3-Piece): Universal Resonance – attracted toward nearest Universe. Physical Armor Class: 500 Spiritual Armor Class: 500 Quality: Mythical Durability: 100,000,000 of 100,000,000 Effect (Active): Void Strider – the stillness of the Void quiets your body making detection difficult for five minutes. Usable once per hour. Description: Blue grey slippers. Only Abyssal Lords can survive, navigate, and alter the void. These pants, through long use, have absorbed an Abyssal Lord’s power. “True God help me,” Ruwen said. “What?” Sift asked. Ruwen turned his attention to Sift and raised his arms with the clothes. “These are the most powerful robes I’ve ever seen, and they come from something called an Abyssal Lord.” Sift threw his clothes into his dimensional belt and reached for the new robes. “Seriously? Blapy gave me something good?” “Much better than good. It looks like they absorb half of any damage you take, make you silent and undetectable, and give you some type of danger sense. And the set bonus is something about detecting other universes, which probably isn’t going to do much for you right now but raises a million questions about where these robes came from that they would have such an ability.” Sift studied the jacket, pants, and boots for a few moments before dressing. “These things are huge. Whoever they came from was a big dude. I wonder where Blapy got them?” “Well, if I had to guess, I’d say from an Abyssal Lord.” “Do you know what that is?” “No idea. I’ll ask Rami about it at home.” Sift slid the jacket over his head, and it looked like he’d pulled on a tent, but as soon as it touched his skin, the garment adjusted until it fit him perfectly. “That’s what I’m talking about,” Sift said. Five seconds later, the pants and slippers were also on, and it looked tailored for Sift specifically. He disappeared. Ruwen’s eyes widened in shock. He could no longer see or detect Sift with any of his senses. “Say something,” Ruwen said. After a second of silence, he created a party and added Sift. Over Chat, Ruwen asked again. Are you talking? Yeah, you can’t hear me? It’s like you don’t exist...wait, I hear a tiny bit of air movement. That’s because I’m waving my arms, Sift replied. Wow, these robes are powerful. You seriously can’t see me? Wait a second, let me try something else. Ruwen triggered Harmonic Sight and immediately noticed the dark silhouette of Sift as a dead area free of vibrations. Ruwen engaged Harmony and Sift became far more visible. Sift punched at Ruwen’s solar plexus and he slapped it away. I thought you said you couldn’t see me, liar. I can’t. Harmony can. You’re not on my map either, and I can’t hear your heartbeat or anything. That cloaking might be better than peak Divinity shielding. Hit me, Sift said. Ruwen immediately jabbed a spear at Sift’s shoulder joint. And Sift reacted faster than normal, allowing him to block Ruwen’s strike. How fast was that? Sift asked. Ruwen shrugged. Maybe forty percent. You reacted faster than normal though. It’s that Void Whisper passive. I couldn’t tell what was coming, but I could feel where it would land. Try seventy percent speed. Ruwen used Harmony to verify Sift’s position and snapped a punch at Sift’s chest. Once again, Sift reacted faster than normal, but the strike still hit him in the arm. Sift rubbed his arm and winced, even though the armor had absorbed half the force. Ruwen grimaced as the shockwave from his punch jostled all the nearby armor and caused a couple of sets to fall off their stands. Sift scanned the disturbed armor. You’re in so much trouble. What? You’re the one that told me to punch you. This is half your fault. I’m invisible for another four and half minutes. Have fun explaining to Fluffy how you wrecked his displays. A portal opened, and Ruwen guessed it was Fluffy coming to see what had disturbed his lower vault. Ruwen quickly cast Root on Sift, locking his feet in place so he couldn’t get away. Ruwen wondered if Fluffy would find the hidden Sift and Ruwen considered covering Sift in oil or dirt from his Void Band, but decided the extra mess would only make Fluffy angrier. Plus, that stealth buff would only last five minutes, which meant Sift needed to find a place to hide quickly. Ruwen touched the shelf and summoned a portal to his room next to the upper library, entering it as Fluffy emerged from his own portal. The quartermaster would disable portals out of the vault as soon as he arrived and Ruwen hoped he’d acted quickly enough to escape. With a sigh of relief, Ruwen glanced around his room. In a basket just inside the door sat the three copies of the Affinity manual that they’d gotten from the rift quest. Ruwen placed them in his Inventory to study later. Right now, if Sift got caught, he’d try and incriminate Ruwen. A wise man knew when to make an exit, which is exactly what he did. 
 CHAPTER 3 It only took a few breaths for Ruwen to realize the Dungeon Master’s lair would be one of the first places Sift looked for Ruwen to get revenge, so he needed to quickly decide his next destination. Fractal remained in his crystal cocoon contemplating the God Stone. The Dungeon Keeper had entered that state after Ruwen had revealed a new System quest that indicated souls were used for backups in the Outerverse. Hamma and Lylan were still with Ky in the Black Pyramid on some sort of pyramid business. Rami was with Xavier, which left Ruwen by himself. That meant now was a good time to explore an idea he’d contemplated for a while. Hey, Lir, do you know where Talker is? I noticed him a while back at Pour Judgment, but I haven’t seen him since. Consulting the Shattered Sun schedule, I can verify that he is not currently working. Let me check New Slegbotl—I found him at the Savage Seven Society. Savage Seven? As in the chickens that almost killed me? The very same. Ruwen sighed. And what is the Savage Seven Society? It is one of several franchises created by the Savage Seven. Her chin rested on her palms, her elbows acting as sentries guarding her latest creation, which lay half-completed before her. Blapy studied her latest drawing. It, too, brought up very old memories. Memories bursting with terror. Coloring helped, though, and this was the seventeenth drawing of the angel she called Winged Annihilation. Blapy's first vision, a rare ability of her kind, had occurred when she was still a hatchling, and her only protection was the centipedes who treated her like family. She had seen Winged Annihilation. Well, their back anyway. Winged Annihilation had one arm in the air, gripping the sky, and the other lower, grasping the earth. Even now, after all these years, it still made her heart thump, and triggered a primal desire to flee. Blapy had spent her life on the lookout for this being. She now believed he would come from the Outerverse, and she couldn't determine if he was friend or foe. If the figure was an enemy, Blapy feared all their hard work would be for nothing. As strong as Ruwen Starfield had become, he paled in comparison to the man she’d glimpsed. This was a vision Blapy had kept to herself. Not from a desire for secrecy but from a superstition that speaking of it would cause it to manifest. Which is why Blapy loved drawing. Blapy admired the stick figure which clutched a storm cloud drawn with the color TIMBERWOLF. The other hand gripped earth the color of BURNT SIENNA. This picture would take forever if Blapy remained so indecisive about the hair. She still had to color the eight wings on the man's back, four to a side. She’d taken a shine to Fractal from the beginning, but the little genius had become something of a son to her, and she’d missed him terribly. “Finally done napping, I see,” Blapy said. “The expansion is way behind schedule now.” Fractal looked around as if lost. He clutched his latest favorite rock to his chest, and his gem-like eyes found Blapy. A surge of light pulsed from Fractal, and he leapt into Blapy’s waiting arms. She spent five seconds hugging Fractal, and he vibrated in joy. “Well?” Blapy asked. “Out with it.” “Fractal see. Fractal hear. Fractal understand.” Relief flooded Blapy, followed by an immense wave of anticipation. The God Stone could finally be finished. And now Blapy had a good excuse to visit her friends. That caused Blapy to pause. She didn't have friends. She couldn't afford to have them. They always died or left her. Fractal wriggled, trying to get out of Blapy’s grasp and to the fist-sized pile of pebbles and gems she’d brought him. “Treasure!” Fractal shouted. Blapy released Fractal, who immediately ran to sit in front of the pile. He began to study each one carefully, hugging and rubbing them against his crystalline cheeks. Blapy smiled. It was true. There was treasure here. “Now don't take all day. You've already been lazing around in that crystal cocoon for darkness knows how long. Some of us have been working our tails off picking up the slack.” Blapy grinned as Fractal excitedly went through the new rocks, completely oblivious to her. She walked over and knelt beside him. Blapy placed her small hand over the sapphire Fractal intently studied, and he looked up at her. “Great job, Fractal. No one else in the universe could've figured the God Stone out. I'm very proud of you.” Fractal met Blapy's gaze, the facets of his eyes reflecting her face thousands of times. “Welcome,” Fractal said. He held up the sapphire. “Thank you.” “I'm going to go tell our…” Blapy trailed off, unsure how to finish that sentence. “Friends?” Fractal finally finished. Blapy’s chest tightened. “Yeah, our friends.” Blapy stood and pointed a finger at Fractal. “I've updated the expansion schedules, so you better get busy. I better not find you racing around the dungeon.” At the word “race,” Fractal went very still, and Blapy wanted to slap herself. “Race,” Fractal said excitedly. “Focus,” Blapy said. “All your racing friends are on a trip. I'm going to find out how much longer they'll be gone.” “Swifty, pony, purple,” Fractal chanted repeatedly. Blapy pinched the bridge of her nose. Fractal loved racing Sift, the Steed of the Apocalypse Vex, and Xavier. “Stop it!” Blapy said. “I’m going for them. Do your chores though.” Fractal ran around the pile of gems, yelling “Swifty, pony, purple” over and over again. “Ugh, you drive me crazy,” Blapy said. “I’m going.” Blapy picked up her picture and carefully replaced PERIWINKLE to its home. She closed the golden carrying case and placed it in her personal vault along with the picture, which she’d finish later. With a final frown and glare at Fractal, which had zero effect on the dungeon keeper, Blapy suppressed her smile and created a dimensional tunnel. It was time to visit some friends.
